translation_notes: context shim: the six package-relative imports of the dispatch classes (.entity, .iri, .quantity, .string, .text, .time) point to a local kif_shim.py holding minimal stand-ins with the attributes the region reads; 'from ... import namespace as NS' -> local namespace.py re-exporting rdflib's XSD; 'from ...rdflib import Literal, URIRef' -> 'from rdflib import ...' (that is what kif_lib.rdflib re-exports). Identical for both sides.
URIRef(expr) -> formatted IRI island f<{expr}> (ldpy's firi does no percent-encoding and no base is declared, so it is exactly URIRef(str(expr)))

Literal(str(self.amount), datatype=NS.XSD.decimal) -> f"{self.amount}"^^xsd:decimal; the f-string replaces str() (identical for Decimal, whose __format__ with an empty spec is str) and the datatype becomes a declared prefixed name. Same for the xsd:dateTime branch.

two of the six term constructors have no island form and stay plain Python: Literal(self.content, self.language) (the @lang suffix requires a literal tag, a variable tag cannot be written) and Literal(self.content) (outside a g{} island there is no bare-literal notation; f{expr} would be node() coercion, not Literal())
the namespace import disappears from the ldpy side, absorbed by the @prefix declaration
